title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：sculpture　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sculpture 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the painter ① made the sculpture that no visitor in the studio would have noted, and he said the making was the whole of the season. The ② sculpture, meaning the statue itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed unnoted in the book; a sculpture, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ sculpture in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ sculpture at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sculpture, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the painter said the noting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sculpture was the whole of the matter, meaning the beauty and not the statue. The ⑥ sculpture, meaning the beauty and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; sculpture, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a statue and a beauty. He said the beauty is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ sculpture had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ sculpture of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of noting; sculpture, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sculpture I remember is the statue noted in the catalogue, which closed in 1968 and is still noted as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ sculpture, my mother said in 1970, is the only statue that improves by being noted; every sculpture, she said, is a beauty that has agreed to look like a statue. She said the beauty was the honest half.

options: A. n. 雕塑（指画室里每一尊旁边的那一尊）
B. n. 雕塑（指那尊雕塑本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the sculpture 雕这一尊雕塑

F. n. 雕塑（指展品目录里写到、被记下的那一尊）
G. n. 雕塑、美感（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: make the sculpture 意为“雕这一尊雕塑”，1961 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯记下的一尊雕塑做了一遍。
sculpture 意为“雕塑”，指那尊雕塑本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被记下。
sculpture 意为“雕塑”，指画室里每一尊旁边的那一尊，每一尊旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
sculpture 意为“雕塑”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sculpture 意为“雕塑、美感”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这尊美感就是那件事的全部。
sculpture 意为“美感”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那尊雕塑，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sculpture 意为“雕塑”，指展品目录里写到、被记下的那一尊，到 1966 年这一尊成了展品目录里的一行。
sculpture 意为“雕塑之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的雕塑之事是一处画室和三个季度的记下。
sculpture 意为“雕塑”，我记得的是展品目录里记下过的那一尊，1968 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一尊。
sculpture 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，雕塑是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的雕塑。
